findings.cross_file_justification: The newly declared review-catch-only arms enter ablation-report.py's component decisions, but Analysis.primaries() also requires a build-task metric for them.
findings.description: The new review-only components cannot reach remove/simplify decisions because their primary metrics include hidden_test_pass_rate, although their task_types prohibit collecting build results.
findings.failure_mode: Even with complete review-catch results demonstrating equivalent defect detection and reduced cost, the build comparison has zero pairs. usable() remains false and nopair forces an inconclusive decision, preventing the report from evaluating the intended simplifications.
findings.suggested_fix: Select primary metrics according to arm applicability: review-catch-only components should require defect_catch_rate without requiring hidden_test_pass_rate. Add a report case with complete review-only results that reaches remove/simplify.

findings.description: Excluding eval_only arms from components also excludes a1_full_openmount from detail_arms, removing the open-versus-closed mount comparison from the report.
findings.failure_mode: A batch can successfully collect the open-mount control trials, but the report emits no per-arm results or comparison for that control. The evaluation-only A/B therefore cannot be assessed from the generated report.
findings.suggested_fix: Maintain separate collections for decision components and reported arms. Exclude eval_only arms from shipped-default decisions while retaining their metrics and comparison against a1_full.

findings.cross_file_justification: The suite diff adds three review-catch-only decision arms (a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only, a1_no_dissent) and the components filter in build() now admits them, but the decision path they flow into (Analysis.primaries()/decide(), same file, untouched) has no review-only branch.
findings.description: The component filter admits the three new review-catch-only arms as decision components, but primaries() still assigns every component both hidden_test_pass_rate and defect_catch_rate. These arms never run build tasks, so the pass-rate comparison always has n == 0, usable() is false and nopair is true. decide() therefore can never return remove or simplify for them; the only reachable outcomes are inconclusive, or investigate/keep from defect_catch_rate. The report is the instrument FR-5 adds these arms for, and it is structurally unable to decide them, while the AR-12 test only checks that nine decision lines exist, not that they can resolve.
findings.failure_mode: After a full batch, the report emits inconclusive decisions for a1_review_only and a1_no_dissent regardless of how large the defect_catch_rate effect is, and the expected-false-positive sentence counts nine components although only six can actually produce a remove/simplify decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Give primaries() a review-only branch: when an arm's task_types is exactly [review-catch], the primary set is [defect_catch_rate] alone (and compute efp over the number of actual comparisons, or document that review-only arms count as one comparison). Add a report test with a review-catch-only arm that has a clear defect_catch_rate deficit and assert the decision is remove.

findings.cross_file_justification: build() excludes only the CONTROL and BARE constants (a0_bare, a1_full) plus eval_only arms; the new a0_bare_fable arm is a second bare baseline (loa_mount: false, phases [BARE]) but is not excluded, so it is reported as a component.
findings.description: a0_bare_fable is a bare-model baseline on the review model, not a shipped component, yet the components list treats it as one. The report will emit a keep/remove/simplify decision for 'component a0_bare_fable' and count it in the expected-false-positive arithmetic (the AR-12 fixture now asserts 9 components including it).
findings.failure_mode: The Method section tells the reader a 'remove' decision was reached for a baseline that cannot be removed, and the false-positive budget is inflated by a non-component comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude arms whose toggles set loa_mount: false (or whose phases are exactly [BARE]) from components, and surface a0_bare_fable in the H1-style baseline section next to a0_bare instead.

findings.description: a1_full_openmount is excluded from components by the new eval_only filter and, per the reviewer's trace, is not in detail_arms either, so none of its rows are rendered anywhere in the report. The arm exists specifically to A/B the open mount against the closed mount (a1_full) on defect_catch_rate; without a report surface the batch spends budget on trials whose result nobody can read without hand-querying rows.
findings.failure_mode: The open-mount leakage A/B runs in every batch and produces no visible output; operators cannot tell whether the closed mount changed defect_catch_rate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Evaluation controls' section that reports eval_only arms against CONTROL on defect_catch_rate with the same interval machinery, explicitly labelled as not a decision; or document that another tool renders them and add a test asserting the arm appears there.

findings.description: The four new arms are appended to arms but the diff does not touch the suite's priority list or the rules comment ('over 6 components'). If run-ablation.sh derives its default arm set from priority, the new arms are never scheduled unless --arms names them, and the AR-12 test asserts the Method section quotes the rules block verbatim, so a stale '6 components' sentence would ship in every report beside the new 'over 9 components' sentence. This could not be confirmed from the diff alone and should be checked before merge.
findings.failure_mode: Default batches collect no data for a0_bare_fable/a1_review_only/a1_no_dissent, and the report contradicts itself about the component count.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the three non-eval_only arms to priority (and decide explicitly whether a1_full_openmount belongs in the default set), and update the rules comment to the new component count.

findings.description: The eval_only exit 2 sits after the applicability branch has computed its REFUSAL (not declared / absent / inapplicable task type) but before that refusal is recorded. For a manual invocation of a1_full_openmount on a build task outside the batch context, the operator sees only 'eval_only arm outside an evaluation batch' and never learns the arm is also inapplicable to the task type. Inside the batch the ordering is harmless because the context variable is set.
findings.failure_mode: Misleading diagnostics on manual runs: the operator sets LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1 to get past the refusal and then hits a second, previously hidden refusal.
findings.suggested_fix: Report both reasons: if a REFUSAL is already set, print it alongside the eval_only line before exit 2, or move the eval_only check ahead of the applicability check so the more general gate is reported first and consistently.

findings.description: The dry-run sandbox line re-implements apply_arm_toggles' config-edit mapping as an inline jq expression, and validate-suite.sh hardcodes TOGGLE_VALUES rather than deriving the vocabulary from lib/sandbox-mount.sh the way it derives rule ids from took-effect.sh. Both are second copies of the toggle semantics; a future toggle added to apply_arm_toggles will be rejected by the validator and misreported by --dry-run until someone remembers to update three places.
findings.failure_mode: A new or changed toggle in lib/sandbox-mount.sh silently drifts from what --dry-run prints and from what validate-suite.sh accepts, so the dry run stops being a faithful preview and the validator blocks valid suites.
findings.suggested_fix: Have apply_arm_toggles expose a pure 'plan' mode (or a shared function in lib/sandbox-mount.sh returning the key=value edits for a toggles JSON) and use it from both the dry run and the validator; or at minimum add a bats case that diffs the dry-run config_edits against the keys actually written to the sandbox .loa.config.yaml for every arm in the committed suite.
